name: HOUR
description: HOUR extracts the hour (0-23) from a time or date-time serial number, reading only the fractional time portion of the value.
tldr: Returns the hour portion (0-23) of a time value.

parameters.name: serial_number
parameters.description: A date-time serial (or a time fraction). The integer part is a date and the fractional part is the time; the hour is taken from the fractional part.

basicExample.description: Get the hour from a time
basicExample.explanation: TIME(12,30,0) is 12:30 PM, so HOUR returns 12.

advancedExamples.title: Extract hour from a date-time serial
advancedExamples.description: HOUR reads the fractional time part
advancedExamples.explanation: The .75 fraction equals 18:00 (6 PM), so HOUR returns 18.

advancedExamples.title: Midnight returns 0
advancedExamples.scenario: A date with no time component
advancedExamples.description: A whole-number serial has no time fraction
advancedExamples.explanation: 45305 is exactly midnight 2024-01-15; with no time fraction HOUR returns 0.

howItWorks: HOUR takes the fractional part of the serial (the time-of-day component) and multiplies it by 24, then returns the integer hour from 0 (midnight) to 23 (11 PM). The date portion is ignored.

howToSteps.name: Reference a time value
howToSteps.text: Point HOUR at a cell or expression that holds a time or date-time.

limitations: HOUR ignores the date portion entirely.
A value with no time fraction (a whole number) returns 0, which can look wrong if you expected a time.
It accepts only valid serials; text times must be converted first.

commonErrors.cause: The argument is text that Excel cannot parse as a time.
commonErrors.fix: Convert the text to a real time serial first (e.g. with TIMEVALUE).

commonErrors.cause: The serial is a whole number with no time part.
commonErrors.fix: Make sure the value actually contains a time fraction.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: HOUR works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Does HOUR work on a full date-time?
faq.answer: Yes, it reads only the time fraction, e.g. 2024-01-15 18:00 returns 18.

faq.question: What about times after 23:59?
faq.answer: Times are stored as fractions under 1, so the maximum hour returned is 23.

faq.question: Why do I get 0 for a date?
faq.answer: Dates without a time component have a zero fraction, so the hour is 0.
